title: Finish it right: the surgeon's knot and the two-step crimp

say: Finish it right: the surgeon's knot and the two-step crimp.
This is the video for module two of Bead Making and Simple Crafts: guided practice with bracelets, necklaces and bead bags.
In beadwork, the finish decides the quality. Most homemade stretch bracelets break because the cord was not pre-stretched, the knot was wrong, or the knot sat against a sharp bead edge.

say: A crimp done well holds for years. Done badly, it slides open and drops every bead on the floor.

say: Put one tiny dot of jewellery cement on the knot. Quick superglue can make elastic hard and brittle, and that is where it snaps. Slide the knot inside a bead, trim to about 3 mm, and let it dry flat for a few hours.

panel.rule: Pre-stretch first. Use jewellery cement, not quick superglue.

say: Thread one crimp tube onto the wire, then the loop of the clasp.

panel.heading: Crimping a clasp in two steps
items: Crimp tube, then the clasp loop
Wire back down through the tube
Back notch: make the groove
Front notch: fold it in half
Tug hard. If it moves, redo it

say: Bring the short end back down through the tube, so both wires lie side by side. Leave a tail of about 3 cm and a small, loose loop around the clasp.

panel.heading: Crimping a clasp in two steps
items: Crimp tube, then the clasp loop
Wire back down through the tube
Back notch: make the groove
Front notch: fold it in half
Tug hard. If it moves, redo it

say: Place the tube in the back notch of the crimping pliers, the one with a dip, nearest the handle. Check the wires are not crossed, and squeeze. Now there is a groove.

panel.heading: Crimping a clasp in two steps
items: Crimp tube, then the clasp loop
Wire back down through the tube
Back notch: make the groove
Front notch: fold it in half
Tug hard. If it moves, redo it

say: Turn the tube a quarter turn, place it in the front notch, the round one, and squeeze to fold it in half.

panel.heading: Crimping a clasp in two steps
items: Crimp tube, then the clasp loop
Wire back down through the tube
Back notch: make the groove
Front notch: fold it in half
Tug hard. If it moves, redo it

say: Tug the wire and clasp hard. If anything moves, cut it off and redo it with a new crimp. Flattening a crimp with ordinary pliers is the mistake that drops beads on the floor.

panel.rule: Never flatten a crimp with ordinary pliers.

say: Before you crimp the second end, hold the necklace up in a curve. Leave a little ease, about the width of half a bead, so it drapes softly. Open jump rings by twisting one side towards you and one away. And put a smooth bead on each side of a sharp crystal.

panel.heading: Right way, wrong way
left: Leave half a bead of ease
right: Pull the wire tight like a bangle
Pull rings apart into a C shape
Let elastic rub a sharp hole

say: Do not pull the wire so tight that the necklace stands stiff like a bangle. Do not pull rings open into a C shape, which weakens the metal. And do not let elastic rub on a sharp hole.

say: Bead bags often use right-angle weave. Each unit is a small square of 4 beads.

panel.heading: Right-angle weave in brief
items: Each unit is a square of 4 beads
Two needles cross inside one bead
Then 2 beads right, 1 bead left, cross
Keep tension even: squares, not diamonds
Make and measure a test square first

say: Put a needle on each end of about 2 metres of line. Pick up 4 beads and cross the needles through the fourth bead.

panel.heading: Right-angle weave in brief
items: Each unit is a square of 4 beads
Two needles cross inside one bead
Then 2 beads right, 1 bead left, cross
Keep tension even: squares, not diamonds
Make and measure a test square first

say: Then pick up 2 beads on the right needle and 1 on the left, and cross again through the outer bead. Repeat.

panel.heading: Right-angle weave in brief
items: Each unit is a square of 4 beads
Two needles cross inside one bead
Then 2 beads right, 1 bead left, cross
Keep tension even: squares, not diamonds
Make and measure a test square first

say: Pull each cross firmly and evenly. If your units look like diamonds instead of squares, your pulls are uneven.

panel.heading: Right-angle weave in brief
items: Each unit is a square of 4 beads
Two needles cross inside one bead
Then 2 beads right, 1 bead left, cross
Keep tension even: squares, not diamonds
Make and measure a test square first

say: Before a bag, weave a 5 by 5 test square and measure it. Then you can plan the size and buy the right number of beads.

say: To remember. Pre-stretch elastic. Surgeon's knot: right over left twice, left over right once. Crimp in two steps, back notch then front notch, and tug-test every crimp. Leave a little ease. And always weave a test square before you plan a bag.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Pre-stretch elastic before stringing
Right over left twice, left over right once
Back notch, front notch, then tug-test
Leave a little ease for a soft drape
Test square before planning a bag

say: Now practise. Make two stretch bracelets and compare them after five days. Practise five crimps on scrap wire. Make a princess necklace with matching earrings. And weave a test square, then a coaster.
